summary: S 0.70 spider: base (ground), body snapped on (2 front fingers + rear tab), spine with open-top journal slots, 4 printed cranks capped by the drive unit (1-3) and the holder post (4), 3 idlers and transfer, N10 drive unit, 2S3P AG13 holder, 8 legs on crank pins; cranks 2/3 2.6 further apart (cad/robot/fitcheck/check.py: 0 failing of 319 with the real cad/legs parts, LEG_PATH 0.5).

parts.name: base
parts.role: ground: bowl with 8 open-top leg windows sized from the real cad/legs neck sweep (NR 5.4, about Ø10.8), front snap ribs, back-sheet pocket, 1.2 pads where loaded (100 % of each window ring), front-window reliefs
parts.why_separate: the ground shell, prints in one piece

parts.name: body
parts.role: dome with the eye block (0.85 leg-arm pocket on its lower front corners), front snap fingers (0.8 x 5, L 8), rear snap tab, inner pocket over the cell pack's lift path
parts.print_orient: rim up (roof on the bed), fingers vertical

parts.name: spine
parts.role: two gear walls with open-top journal slots (TURN), idler-axle holes, keel seat; wall tops raised 0.8 under the holder post where idler 3's tip passes
parts.why_separate: carries the whole train as one unit
parts.print_orient: keel down, walls upright, slots up

parts.name: crankshafts
parts.role: 4 printed cranks with gears, webs and Ø3 pins
parts.print_orient: axis vertical, one piece; support marks sanded (sandpaper)

parts.name: idlers
parts.role: 3 idlers and the transfer compound, each GW - 0.4 wide, turning (TURN, Ø3.7 bore) on printed spacer sleeves Ø3.2 x 3.5 (M2-tapped bore Ø1.6, wall 0.8) clamped wall to wall by the M2 axle, so tightening does not pinch the walls

parts.name: drive-unit
parts.role: N10 clamp, transfer cheek, 2 blocks + ears; wall-top cheeks whose tongues cap cranks 1-3; two lugs on its -x plate clamped by idler axles 1 and 2 (STEEL holes, 1.2 wall); ear 2 lowered to 1.0 tall (the holder tab and its M2 head sit under the N10 and the lower clamp)
parts.why_separate: motor comes out without the train

parts.name: pinion
parts.role: 16 T m 0.6 pinion pressed on the N10's D-shaft (DSHAFT), meshes the transfer big gear

parts.name: legs
parts.role: 8 legs, end tube on the pin, ball in the window

parts.name: cell-holder
parts.role: 3 x 2 AG13, spring, nickel strip, wire slot; the post (x ±4, y ±3 about the cells' centre) down to the wall tops, post-cap tongues cap crank 4; front tab (5.2 x 1.2) on drive ear 2 (lowered, under the N10 and its clamp) with the holder M2 (hole STEEL, head on the tab) down into drive block 2 / ear 2; front-bottom notch at drive block 2; 0.8 leg-arm pocket on its top edge
parts.why_separate: screwed to drive block 2, cells swap

parts.name: m2-screws
parts.role: M2 socket cap ISO 4762 (1.5 mm hex key), self-tapping in PLA (pilot Ø1.6, assumed, proven on coupon c2, the holder's too): 3 idler axles (1 and 2 through the drive unit's lugs), 2 keel, 1 holder

joints.name: crank-in-spine
joints.apart_by: lift the holder and the drive unit, lift each crank out of its slots

joints.name: gear-mesh
joints.in_from: +z (idler drops in, then its M2 axle along +x)
joints.apart_by: pull the M2 axle along -x, lift the idler

joints.name: leg-on-pin
joints.in_from: -z through its open-top window, then along the pin (x)
joints.apart_by: lift the body, slide the leg off its pin along x, lift it out

joints.name: drive-on-spine

held.+x: lug face on the -x wall, axle heads
held.-x: lugs clamped by idler axles 1 and 2
held.+z: idler axles 1 and 2 through the lugs

joints.in_from: +z (on the bench, before the idler axles)
joints.apart_by: undo idler axles 1 and 2 along -x (spine set out of the base), lift the drive unit

joints.name: holder-on-drive-block

held.+x: tab on drive ear 2, post tongues in slot 4
held.-x: tab on drive ear 2, post tongues in slot 4
held.+y: tongues in slot 4, M2 in the block
held.-y: tongues in slot 4, M2 in the block
held.+z: M2 (head on the tab) into drive block 2 / ear 2
held.-z: tab on the ear top, post on the wall tops

joints.apart_by: slide the N10 out (-x), undo the M2 (from above), lift the holder

joints.name: body-front-snaps
joints.apart_by: pull the body up (45 deg return faces)

joints.name: spacer-on-axle
joints.in_from: +z (sleeve in the idler, then the M2 along +x)

dropped through its window, slid onto its pin along x, ball in its seat

on the bench: pressed on the N10 shaft to its stop, flat to the D
slid in along +x with its pinion over the holder tab, pinion meshes, flush; comes out along -x with the holder in place
+ toward the strip, each cell pressed against its spring as it goes down

alternatives.choice: 2 snap fingers at x ±6 under base ribs

alternatives.choice: pocket + outward bulge, 45° chamfer under it; through only where the bulge would come within LEG_PATH of a leg

open-top journal slots capped by drive-unit tongues (1-3) and the holder post (4)

≤ 1.1 % across layers; fits.PRESS kept as assumed

alternatives.choice: PY +0.4 with a 0.38 notch and a body inner pocket

alternatives.choice: local pocket PKR 0.85 from the arms' 24-pose sweep

acceptance.text: the parts are imported from cad/legs, cad/eyes, cad/base, cad/body; scale, crank and leg path from cad/motion.py, never copied
the parametric parts may be reshaped where the inside needs it (surfaces moved, stretched or opened), as long as the robot's look passes the judge

every part, screw and contact is in the code that counts the fit; a fit that leaves something out is reported as partial. Wires take no volume (flexible, routed by hand); only a hole or slot where a wire must pass a wall between its two ends (Morante, 2026-11-21: «no consideres los cables ni el espacio que ocupan… si hay que conectar cables entre dos puntos que separa una pared, sí tienes que dejar un agujero o ranura para que pasen»)
assembly order and each part's path checked before the scale
the motor's fit is a separate, screwed part (the motor is bought later and measured; a fix reprints grams)
Morante can change the cells; the switch is reached from outside
two 5 mm LED bores in the eyes, wired by Morante (no eyes board)
the views command renders the robot and jenscolt's assembled meshes in the same views and framing, written as images/reference.png next to the photos
fasteners: start with M2 self-tapping screws or snap fits; M3 where it solves a problem
margins, walls and clearances: the standard values of cad/fits.py; changed only where they cause a problem, and put to Morante
print support as little as possible; up to 20-30 % on a part is accepted when a valid solution needs it
screwdriver access: where it blocks a solution, it is put to Morante before the solution is dropped

when something collides: first layout; then the colliding part is reshaped locally to make room (a pocket, relief, notch or bulge), any bulge outward on the shell (base) or the body first; a larger S is not wanted and is only put to Morante when nothing else works (Morante, 2026-11-21: «cada vez que te encuentres con un problema de colisiones, modifica o deforma la pieza local para dar cabida a lo que falta… empiezas por fuera en la carcasa o en el cuerpo»; «no quiero aumentar la escala más»)

views.py places jenscolt's meshes (body, base, eyes, sensor, 8 legs; leg placement as the archived tools/assemble_jenscolt.py) at the robot's S and frame, writes out/reference.stl, and renders robot and reference with tools/mesh_ref.py views; `views.py --reference` writes images/reference.png; meshes are read only here, never by build.py or a gate
cell contacts: conical springs + nickel strip (to buy)
eye LEDs: red or yellow from the Arduino kit, with their resistors placed and counted
wiring through one 3-pin JST-XH (to buy); hook-up wire from the Arduino kit

crank 4 and the rear legs clear the base's back sheet through a local pocket in it, 1.6 mm outward, x ±11, z 7-17, hidden behind the body's rear tab (notched to match); the back scoop itself is not moved (Morante, 2026-11-21: «Tu recomendación»)

cranks 2 and 3 (and their mirror) 2.6 mm further apart along Y than motion.py's uniform DY, standard fits.LEG_PATH on every leg pair (no waiver); the middle legs open ~1.3 mm each, shown to Morante next to jenscolt before motion.py changes (Morante, 2026-11-21: «Ok», S 0.70 signed probe: leg ends 2/3 −2.55)
front leg windows of the base: a local relief where the leg arm passes (S 0.70 probe −0.76 at ±20.6, −16.9, 16.3) (Morante, 2026-11-21: «Ok»)
leg-arm end tube tail shortened to ~0.7 mm where it meets its own crank web (Morante, 2026-11-21: «Ok»)
body held at the front by snap fits (the front screws are boxed in by the eye block and the legs); screws only where they have driver access (Morante, 2026-11-21: «Ok»)
a probe that leaves parts out reported as a fit
jenscolt's inner posts in the body or base

full cad_verify PASS with every part inside (no collision over the 24 poses, each part's assembly path) at the chosen S, and the judge >= 0.60 against jenscolt's model (his photos and his assembled meshes in the same views as the robot)
front snaps click on and pull off by hand; legs walk a full turn
snap coupon, runs before the body and the base are printed (PRESS assumed): front-wall strip with rib + rim strip with fingers, rear-tab rib, real print orientations; clicks on, pulls off by hand

gear and slot coupon m 0.6 (c2 + c3 merged): wall-pair stub with open-top slots, cap tongue, a drive-unit lug, a crank and an idler (GW - 0.4 wide) on its spacer sleeve and a real M2 self-tapping axle (pilot Ø1.6, assumed); turns by hand, no skip, drops in, turns free, cap holds, lug clamped, tightening does not pinch; plus the holder tab (1.2 thick, hole STEEL) on a drive-ear stub over a block stub, real M2 into pilot Ø1.6 (assumed): holds, head clear
leg coupon: leg end bore on a printed Ø3 pin + window strip; slides on, ball seats, swings free; the pin is printed in the crank's real orientation (axis vertical)

diagram: base > keel M2 > spine set (spine, cranks in open slots, idlers, drive-unit caps 1-3, 3 M2 axles: 1 and 2 through its lugs) > legs (window, pin) > cell-holder (post on the wall tops, tongues cap 4, tab M2 into drive block 2) > N10 + pinion > cells > lid; body snaps
